memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'The one who touches any such thing will be unclean till evening. He
must not eat any of the sacred offerings unless he has bathed himself
with water. When the sun goes down, he will be clean, and after that
he may eat the sacred offerings, for they are his food'"
- Lev 22:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice how the passage ends. Yes, the priest was unclean - but only
till evening. Yes, he had to wash - but then he ate. Uncleanness in
Leviticus was almost never permanent. There was nearly always a way
back.

That is the quiet mercy running underneath all these regulations. God
did not build a system designed to keep people out. He built one that
kept showing them the way back in.

Dear reader, please hold on to this if you have failed recently. Your
sin, confessed and brought to Christ, does not define your permanent
address. Water and evening always came. In the New Covenant something
far greater has come - the blood of Christ, which cleanses us from all
sin (1 John 1:7).

The old washing had to be repeated endlessly. Christ's cleansing was
once for all (Heb 10:14). Peter learned this at the last supper, when
Jesus told him that a person who has bathed needs only to wash their
feet (John 13:10). The full washing has happened. Daily confession is
the foot-washing of an already-clean child.

The sun goes down. Morning comes. Grace is not in short supply.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I living as though a past failure has permanently marked me?
2. Do I understand the difference between Christ's once-for-all
   cleansing and daily confession?
3. What do I need to bring to God tonight before the day ends?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that there is always a way back to You through Jesus.
Wash me tonight, and let me rise tomorrow knowing I am fully Yours.
Amen.
